data.title: Chat: residual existence oracles for hidden channels — DM 403 type-marking + threadRoot cross-conversation probe (document or close)

data.body: Found during AS-6 review (does not violate any AS-6 criterion; recording per my blocks-vs-backlog sort). Two probes let a non-member infer that SOME hidden conversation exists, without confirming #board specifically: (1) getMessages/postMessage/markRead on a DM you are not in returns 403 'forbidden' while hidden channels and nonexistent ids return 404 — so with sequential conversation ids, an allocated id that 404s is identifiable as a hidden channel (the AS-6 plan section 7.3 claims an id gap is indistinguishable from a DM; the 403 makes DMs distinguishable). Same class existed pre-AS-6 on write paths; AS-6 deviation 3 extended it to the read path. (2) postMessage to a visible channel with threadRoot = an invisible message id says 'belongs to a different conversation' vs 'Unknown thread root message' for a nonexistent id — reveals invisible message ids exist (wording identical for DM vs board messages, so no attribution). Options: accept + document in apps/chat/README.md threat-model note, or normalize DM non-member reads to 404, or randomize/decouple ids. CTO call; low urgency — both are within the plan's accepted residual class (section 0 exception 2 + 7.3).
